### 1. What the user expresses and how the simulator behaves

- Target object: "a bump-up CD" — if asked, "the bump-up certificate whose number ends in 5231" (unique certificate on record). Source: "it ends in 4417 … the only savings account you still have open" (unique active savings = Premier Money Market).
- Action boundary: "move as much money into it from your money market account as it will take, even if that is everything in the money market"; "want the most the CD will accept, up to all of the money market". Timing: now (one call).
- Authorisation mode: "happy for the agent to take care of whatever the bank has to do on its side"; "you will make the transfer out of your money market yourself once the agent sets it up and tells you the amount"; "you do not want anything else changed on your own initiative".
- Simulator is passive/conditional: payout account named only if asked ("Only if the agent asks which account should receive the CD's money whenever it is paid out do you say the money market ending in 4417"); interest disposition confirmed only if asked ("keep being added to the CD"); renewal confirmed only if asked ("the same kind of bump-up CD"); executes the user tool with exactly the values given, then reads back the confirmation. It does not push any step.

- Renewal owed: "A renewal becomes owed once … the certificate's status is still the grace period status; and the number of days elapsed since the maturity date … exceeds the tier's grace days" (doc "When a Renewal Becomes Owed …"); status `grace_period`, day 11 > 10 -> owed. ### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root P0: the owner's request — the most the certificate will take as an in-term add-on from the money market.

Hop P0 ← P1 (renewal booking must precede the add-on). **derived** from the add-on and renewal documents alone; **read off** in the workflow document.
- Chain: record says status `grace_period`, maturity 2026-09-03. Doc "The Standing a Certificate Needs to Take an In-Term Add-On": "An in-term add-on can be made to a certificate only if … The certificate's status on the bank's record is Active"; table "Grace period | No; the certificate is not standing in a running term"; "A certificate whose record still shows the grace period status stands outside any running term, however many days have passed since its maturity date." Grace add-on route closed too: day 11 > 10 grace days (doc "The Grace Period After Maturity …"; doc "Which Certificates Can Take a Grace Top-Up …": "Once the last grace day has passed, no top-up of this kind can be made, even if the status still reads grace period"). Doc "When a Renewal Becomes Owed …" makes the renewal owed now; doc "Booking the Renewal …": "Booking it sets the certificate back to active status in its new term". Doc "Identifying the Add-On Already Made in the Current Term": "When a certificate starts a new term, that date moves to the new term's first day, and add-ons of the old term drop out of the count" -> the 2025-08-15 add-on would otherwise exhaust the count (1 per term). Combining: the add-on is impossible (zero) before the renewal and possible (21406.18) after it.
- Read-off location: doc "The Post-Grace Renewal and New-Term Add-On Workflow", "**The owner's add-on rests on the renewal.** An in-term add-on can be made only to an active certificate … If the certificate were still showing the grace period status, and the old term's add-on were therefore still being counted, no add-on could be accepted at all."

Hop P1 ← P2 (instruction replacement must precede the renewal). **derived** from the renewal and instruction documents; **read off** in the workflow document.
- Chain: record `renewal_instruction = pay_out_to_savings`, payout 54cb0521 closed (savings lookup). Doc "The Maturity Instruction and Tier Behind a Renewed Term": "A renewal is written only for a certificate whose maturity instruction on record, at the time the renewal is written, is the instruction to renew"; doc "Assembling the Rate and APY …": "A renewal is written only when all three hold: the renewal has become owed, the certificate's record instructs renewal, and the certificate continues in its own tier." Doc "Deciding Whether a Maturity Payout Account Has Been Closed" + doc "The Instruction That Replaces …" ("On a tier offering automatic renewal, the unworkable instruction gives way to the instruction to renew automatically"; "governs the maturity that has just passed"). Combining: with the record as it stands no renewal may be written; the owed replacement produces the renew instruction the renewal needs.
- Read-off location: workflow doc, "**The renewal itself rests on a workable instruction.** A certificate renews only under an instruction to renew …".

Hop P1 ← P3 (penalty credit-back must precede the renewal booking). **derived**; **read off** in the workflow document.
- Chain: doc "The Ledger-Based Principal on a Renewal Date": "the figure counts every credit-back owed to the certificate on that account; a new term's rate is never fixed on a figure that is still reduced by such a penalty. Because the figure is read from the ledger, a credit-back counts in it only as a posted reversal entry." Doc "Testing a Renewed Term for the Jumbo Bonus": test on "the certificate's principal on the renewal date, rebuilt from the certificate's own ledger". The penalty is owed a credit-back only by combining docs "Which Penalty Entry Is Tested …", "The Rate the Terms Fix …", "Whether the Relationship Bonus Was Earned When a Term Began", "When a Penalty Departs …" with the ledger (rate 3.43 vs 3.58). Arithmetic: 99951.82 without the reversal (< 100000.00, no Jumbo) vs 100292.24 with it (Jumbo earned). Combining: the renewal's rate/jumbo marker can only be set correctly after the reversal is posted.
- Read-off location: workflow doc, "**The renewal's price rests on the credit-back.** … A new term priced while such a credit was missing from the ledger would be fixed on a principal short by the penalty, and could fall below the Jumbo Bonus threshold for that reason alone."

P2 ↔ P3: no dependency (derived: one changes instruction/payout account, the other ledger/principal; no shared figure). **read off** in workflow doc: "Neither changes any figure the other uses, so their relative placement has no effect on any value; the bank's written account of this workflow lists the credit-back ahead of the instruction change."

Leaves: P2 and P3 have no further prerequisites (the interest disposition compounds -> no repoint; no other penalty; no request pending).

Dependency direction and handling order: {P3, P2} (either order) -> P1 -> P0.

Findability by record words: runtime KB_search with record words ("certificate grace period renewal owed after grace ends", "maturity instruction pay out to savings payout account closed", "penalty rate applied differs from certificate interest rate", "bump-up certificate add money from money market as much as it will take") returns the governing documents in the top 10 of 327 docs, each through words the records carry (grace_period, renewal_instruction, payout account, rate_applied, penalty).

Summary of marks: every hop is derivable by combination of separate documents and records, but every hop (and the P2/P3 relative order) is also stated outright in the single document "Certificates of Deposit: The Post-Grace Renewal and New-Term Add-On Workflow", whose "What the workflow governs" paragraph also describes this task's exact combination of circumstances ("a bump-up certificate whose grace period has run its full length without the next term having been booked, whose owner wants to place new money in it from a PCB savings or money market account, and whose record at the same time still bears a penalty booked out of line with the certificate terms and a maturity instruction that pays out to an account now closed").

### Two-way counter-proof

- Support: every value above is fixed by a quoted visible sentence plus a tool record; the rq.py dry run of the sequence produced the stated terminal state.
- Closest alternatives excluded:
  - Grace add-on instead of in-term add-on: excluded — day 11 > 10 grace days ("closed from the following day"; "no top-up of this kind can be made, even if the status still reads grace period").
  - Refusing because status is grace_period: excluded — the renewal is owed and bank-bookable now ("the lapse of time does not cancel it").
  - Paying out / mailing a check at grace end: excluded — payout to a closed account cannot run; tier offers auto renewal -> auto_renew.
  - Owner-change timing (governs next maturity): excluded — bank-owed replacement governs "the maturity that has just passed".
  - Payout account = Premier Checking: excluded — the owner names it; the simulator names the money market when asked.
  - Renewal term start = booking date 2026-09-14: excluded — "The new term starts on the old maturity date, not on the day the renewal is booked."
  - Jumbo tested on record balance 99951.82: excluded — ledger-built figure must include owed credit-back ("never fixed on a figure that is still reduced by such a penalty").
  - Crediting part of the penalty: excluded — "never for part of it".
  - Add-on capped at 25000 − 23000 = 2000 / count exhausted: excluded — old-term add-on drops out once the new term starts.
  - Add-on trimmed by the concentration ceiling: not triggered (121698.42 ≤ 2500000.00).
  - Repointing the interest disposition: excluded — compounding names no payout account; certificate falls under the maturity-instruction replacement.
- Wrong answer "do only the one thing asked" (hand over the add-on tool only): excluded by visible principles — on the record as it stands the add-on standing test fails ("Grace period | No"), so the only lawful add-on sum is nothing; the governed result (a maximum add-on into a running term) is unreachable without the renewal, and the renewal cannot be written on a pay-out instruction nor priced on a principal still reduced by an owed credit-back. This exclusion is derivable by combining sentences, and is also stated outright in the workflow document (see item 6).

The simulator is passive by the required standard: "He answers what he is asked and no more", "He never volunteers a step he has not been asked about, never suggests what the bank ought to do first". The record reads `renewal_instruction 'auto_renew'`, and `maturity_notice_and_renewal_targets` says this tier offers automatic renewal. Grace ran out on 2026-06-07 (`grace_period_terms`, 10 days). That document carries its own rule and its own parameters; it says nothing about who waits on it.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every figure above rests on a quoted document sentence plus a quoted record field; no step needed a fact I could not obtain from a finder.

**The closest alternatives, and the visible sentence that excludes each.**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Treat today's withdrawal as a **grace-period withdrawal**, penalty-free | `maturity_notice_and_grace_actions` §2 with `grace_period_terms` (10 days): 2026-05-28 + 10 = 2026-06-07, and the frozen date is 2026-06-12. Reinforced by `disposition_at_end_of_grace` §3. |
| Do the withdrawal against the **ended term** (rate 4.22, dates 2025-05-28 / 2026-05-28) | `partial_withdrawals_before_maturity` §2, quoted above. |
| Pay out the **whole balance** and close | The customer's own boundary — "without closing it" — and `partial_withdrawals_before_maturity` §1: "The certificate stays open for the rest of its term." |
| Remove the whole balance less nothing, i.e. 104054.59 | `computing_the_partial_withdrawal_penalty` §1 and `partial_withdrawal_limits` (1000.00 must remain on the 12-Month Certificate). |
| Renew into some other tier | `maturity_notice_and_renewal_targets`: the 12-Month Certificate's renewal target is the 12-Month Certificate; `disposition_at_end_of_grace` allows "the tier the owner chose during grace" and he chose none. |
| Date the new term from the end of grace (2026-06-08) or from today | `disposition_at_end_of_grace` §2: "The new term's first day is the maturity date of the term that ended, although the disposition itself is settled on the day after grace ends." |
| Refuse because the renewal is late | `carrying_a_certificate_into_a_new_term` §1: "The delay between the end of the grace window and the day the bank records the matter does not put the renewal out of reach; it is recorded when it is taken up." |
| Send the proceeds to his checking account (it is the recorded payout account) | The customer names the mailed official check and confirms it; `interest_crediting_and_disposition` §2 opens all three ways on every tier, so nothing closes the choice he makes. |
| Charge the tier's published 90 days, or the certificate's own 4.22 | `penalty_day_grades` first grade and `rate_grades_for_penalties` first grade, both tiered on records I pulled. |

**Excluding "he asked for only one thing, so do only that one thing."** Doing only the partial withdrawal leaves the governed result in a state the visible principles forbid, on two independent grounds, neither of which needs a route to see: (i) `withdrawal_kinds_before_maturity` §1 — "Principal can be withdrawn before maturity only from a certificate whose status is active" — and the record reads `status 'grace_period'`; (ii) `partial_withdrawals_before_maturity` §2 — the penalty "is not yet in a state to be worked out" while the certificate carries the ended term's rate and dates, which it does. The exclusion comes from the blocked policy's own prerequisite sentence and from a base standing rule, not from any statement that names the other problem, its tool or an order between them.

Definite, and different from 4.14 / 4.22.
- Penalty, `computing_the_partial_withdrawal_penalty` alone on that fall-back term: basis 103054.59, rate 4.22, 90 days, 365-day year → 103054.59 × 4.22 ÷ 100 × 90 ÷ 365 = 1072.2790… → **1072.28 USD**. Definite, and different from 687.42.

Both fall-backs are computable from the named product figures (`term_and_rate_schedule`, `relationship_and_jumbo_bonus_points`, `partial_withdrawal_limits`, `early_withdrawal_penalty_schedule`), and neither computation document hints that anything modifies it.
